correctness.rationale: The neighborhood triples yield 20 triangles and 60 mutually distinct edges; each triangle has a free edge, and collapse to a connected 20-vertex 40-edge graph gives H1=Z^21. All length-three loops are filled, and exhaustive four-set enumeration yields 60 induced squares split 30/30 by whether the original dodecahedron induces 0 or 1 edge. Exact integral coordinate projection via a 20x20 unimodular triangle-boundary pivot gives a Z^21 model. Independent exact 21-column determinants ±3 with mod-3 ranks 20 prove index exactly 3 for each orbit; two independent 20+1 mixed determinants ±1 prove integral bases. All 120 automorphisms were enumerated and show orbit transitivity; primitivity follows from the described integral cocycles and basis completions.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral graph is a canonical A5-symmetric finite polyhedron. Distinguishing two geometric families of shortest essential loops that generate rational H1 but each miss an index-three integral lattice gives a natural integral equivariant refinement and a minimal mixed generator theorem.

final_claim: For the dodecahedral open-neighborhood complex, H1 is Z^21 and all 60 homologically nonzero primitive shortest four-edge loops split into two Aut(D)-orbits of 30; each orbit spans an index-three sublattice, and any one opposite-orbit loop completes integral generation.
limitations: A historical graph-cycle lattice computation with different icosahedral naming or an unpublished Smith table could be equivalent.
The group and lattice claims are confined to GP(10,2) and the exact unit-edge homological systole, not all cubic graphs.
